A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their text, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across substantial renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, modality ablations, debiasing experiments, human annotations, and appendix experiments on transfer and modality selection.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds the instruction-tuned model comparison in Section 7, Table 9.

M1.justification: The modality-annotation procedure, BERT/LLaMA-2-7B/SDIF majority-vote debiasing framework, and Appendix 9.11 modality selector remain unchanged. The added instruction-tuned models are evaluation variants, not revisions to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same English MIntRec-1 and MIntRec2.0 tasks, original and debiased datasets, and cross-dataset transfer scenarios. The new instruction-model comparison adds no dataset or task coverage; transfer experiments already appeared in v1 Appendix 9.5.2.

E2.justification: v2 adds LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct as evaluated comparison variants in Section 7, Table 9. These differ from the pretrained and task-fine-tuned variants evaluated in v1. Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds a control comparing prompt-only instruction-tuned textual models with the existing evaluations, specifying shared few-shot prompts and system messages on original and debiased data. This extends the evaluation design; existing splits, metrics, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new fair-comparison ablation tests whether task-specific fine-tuning explains textual models' advantage. The dataset-size control, transfer experiments, modality masking, and error examples already existed in v1 and are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state that small multimodal model results are averaged over five seeds in Appendix 9.4. v2 adds no new run-count information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance testing; Table 9 reports point estimates.

E6.justification: Table 9 adds results for two instruction-tuned models. For example, Mistral-7B-Instruct achieves 64.27% and 39.80% accuracy on original MIntRec-1 and MIntRec2.0, versus 26.85% and 28.65% on their debiased counterparts. These are newly reported settings, not corrections to prior scores. Matched pre-existing numerical tables are unchanged apart from equivalent zero formatting.

T1.justification: The definitions and reasoning underlying modality annotation and textual-bias filtering are retained. No new or revised formal assumptions, mathematical derivations, theorems, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims: textual-model superiority on the original benchmarks, strong textual bias, substantial degradation after debiasing, and the need for better datasets and adaptive fusion. The added evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 7 adds an evidence-based qualification that fine-tuning contributes to performance differences, while textual bias remains a substantial factor. Section 8 also adds loss of temporal information between sampled frames as an error mechanism. The existing limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v1's generic Code/Data hyperlink in Section 5.4 is replaced by an explicit release statement and named GitHub repository in v2's abstract. This makes access information more explicit, without establishing that availability itself is new. Existing hardware, hyperparameters, prompts, and timing information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 expands citations for domain-specific intent applications and adds references concerning crystal-property prediction, entity extraction, and opinion analysis in Appendix 9.1. These contextual additions leave the central positioning around modality bias in intent detection unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized language corrections, expands the main dataset description, summarizes existing transfer findings in Section 7, and swaps the human-annotation and debiasing appendix sections. Most prose and the overall three-phase narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 9, moves v1 Figure 17 into the main text as Figure 2, and regroups existing appendix displays. It also fixes overlapping text in Figure 1 and reformats the before/after chart legend. Existing chart content and table designs are largely preserved.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens v1's largely resource-based defense of unequal training strategies with the empirical control in Section 7, Table 9: prompt-only instruction-tuned textual models still outperform the open-source multimodal LLMs on the original benchmarks. This better supports the bias interpretation without fully isolating differences between model families. Clearer resource access and presentation also help, while the original scientific scope and acknowledged fine-tuning limitations remain.
